newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma breaks 305 level, bonds fall late.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma breaks 305 level, bonds fall late.

text.p: Ecu/drachma continued to cruise higher, breaking through the 305 level before settling at 304.80/00 in late, active dealing while bonds succumbed to profit-taking, traders said.

"The market is short Ecu and tends to over-react when the central bank shows it wants Ecu/drachma higher," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The Bank of Greece managed to fix Ecu/drachma up at the fixing and signalled it was comfortable with even higher levels in its afternoon window."
Other dealers said stop losses were hit, reinforcing the upward trend on Wednesday.
Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos told reporters the central bank's 197 forex policy would be anti-inflationary but much more flexible compared to 1996.
Meanwhile, bond dealers said prices of three-year fixed-coupon bonds and FRNs 2002 and 2003 lost 20 to 35 basis points on profit-taking.

"We have seen some profit-taking in fixed-coupon bonds and FRNs due 2002 and 2003 that has to do with the auction of January 24," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "I would call it a correction."

The finance ministry will auction 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon at 12.40 percent and 120 billion drachma worth of three-year, 10.20-percent coupon bonds on January 24.
Implied drachma forwards held higher morning levels and depos steadied in late dealings, traders said.
The mark was quoted at 156.40/50 drachmas from Wednesday's 155.800 fix, the dollar at 256.08/58 drachmas from 252.230 and the Ecu at 304.40/60 from 302.980 drachmas.
